newsitem.title: JAPAN: PM says he, wife, daughter had no Nomura deals - Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: PM says he, wife, daughter had no Nomura deals - Kyodo.

text.p: Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Tuesday that neither he nor those members of his family still included in his family register had any dealings with Nomura Securities Co Ltd, the brokerage at the centre of widening payoff scandal, Kyodo news agency reported.

"My wife and daughter in my family registry have no accounts," Kyodo quoted Hashimoto as saying. "As for those (daughters) living on their own or married, I don't know because that is their own responsibility."

Household registers in Japan include the names of the husband and wife and children living as part of the household. When daughters get married, their names are stricken from the parents' register and placed in that of their husband.

Hashimoto was replying to reporters' questions after Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference that three ministers in Hashimoto's cabinet currently have dealings with Nomura, but not in stocks and financial products in which they could receive special treatment. He declined to reveal names.
Kyodo said Hashimoto also denied that his office staff had conducted transactions with Nomura on his behalf, saying: "Any secretary who works for me knows I dislike stocks."

The scandal surrounding Nomura, Japan's biggest brokerage, involves illegal compensation of client losses but prosecutors are also investigating possible misdeeds linked to accounts set up for elite customers, including bureaucrats and politicians.
